archiveTake: A chaotic, deeply unserious sci-fi comedy that works best if you’re here for the characters and the nonsense more than the plot.
spoilerFreeReview: I wasn’t the biggest fan of Oz 9 at first. It took a while to get going, and I usually prefer more serious audio dramas. This was basically the exact opposite of that. That said, it does get more interesting after the first season, and I understand why some people really love it. It’s chaotic, unserious, and definitely has its moments. Not for me, but not bad either, just not my style.

However, I couldn’t bring myself to keep listening after episode 94. I felt like the main plotline had mostly ended by around episode 80, and after that the show started to feel directionless. It lost the central story that had been keeping me interested and leaned much more heavily into just goofing off every episode. Some of my favorite characters were also killed off or removed from the main plot, and at that point I didn’t really see a reason to keep listening.

I’d recommend it to someone looking for a goofy, unserious show who doesn’t care that much about having one big overarching plot. But if you want something more serious, or a story that keeps pulling you forward, I probably wouldn’t recommend it.
thoughts: I stuck with Oz 9 for a long time because when it worked for me, it really worked. There are some genuinely funny stretches and characters I got attached to, which is probably why I made it as far as I did.

What eventually lost me wasn’t really the comedy itself, but the feeling that the story no longer had anywhere specific to go. Once that central thread disappeared, the chaos stopped feeling like a break from the plot and started feeling like the whole point.
